parties: Popatlal Fulchand Sundesha (acquirer); Aksh Optifibre Limited (target)
headline: Popatlal Fulchand Sundesha triggers SEBI Takeover Disclosure under Regulation 31(4)
sum: Popatlal Fulchand Sundesha has filed a substantial acquisition disclosure with NSE under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, indicating a acquisition event in Aksh Optifibre Limited. The acquisition and disclosure timing suggest a material shareholding threshold crossing.
implication: Regulation 31(4) disclosure is mandatory upon crossing 25% or 50% shareholding thresholds and triggers open offer obligations within 4 weeks unless exemption applies-assess acquirer intent (strategic vs. financial), exemption grounds (general exemption route under Regulation 10), and public shareholder protection measures.
detail: Popatlal Fulchand Sundesha, as a substantial acquirer, has filed the mandatory disclosure under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI Takeover Code. The filing with NSE indicates a crossing of a material shareholding threshold in Aksh Optifibre, a technology/optronics company. Under the Regulations, such disclosure is triggered at 25%, 50%, 75%, and 90% thresholds, and requires open offer unless a carve-out (general exemption, creeping acquisition exemption at 5% per annum, or preferential allotment exemption) is invoked. The acquirer's obligation to make a public announcement and detailed disclosure includes target business, future plans, financing structure, and terms of the offer.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure upon crossing 25%, 50%, 75%, 90% shareholding thresholds; triggers open offer unless exemption applies.
General exemption from open offer (Reg. 10) for acquirers meeting governance/financial criteria; commonly invoked exemption route.
Creeping acquisition exemption at 5% per annum; allows incremental shareholding without triggering open offer.
Public announcement, detailed disclosure, target directors' opinion, financial/legal advisors' roles, and shareholder meetings; procedural architecture.
Open offer conditions: 4-week tendering window, 90% acceptance threshold, settlement mechanics, and escrow arrangements.
Prohibitions on insider trading during announcement–settlement; disclosure of conflicts; mandatory independent director certification.
Trading windows and disclosure obligations for insiders during acquisition announcement and settlement phases.
Exchange notification and continuous disclosures during material corporate action; dual filing on BSE and NSE.

conditions: Crossing of material shareholding threshold (25%, 50%, 75%, or 90%)
Filing of Regulation 31(4) disclosure with NSE and BSE
Public announcement within 4 working days of threshold crossing (unless exemption claimed)
Determination of exemption status (general exemption, creeping, or preferential allotment)
approvals: SEBI review of exemption claim (if applicable)
Competition Commission of India (CCI) clearance if acquirer is a competition-sensitive entity (if >₹2,500 cr combined turnover)
RBI approval if acquirer is financial services regulated entity
Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) if acquirer is non-resident Indian or NRI
structure.novel: Filing under Regulation 31(4) confirms threshold crossing; exemption route (general exemption vs. open offer mandatory) will drive subsequent mechanics and timeline.

triggers.note: Disclosure filing itself is the trigger; threshold crossing (25%/50%/75%/90%) is the substantive event.
If acquirer meets net worth, stock exchange quotation, and governance criteria, open offer may be exempted.
If combined turnover of acquirer and target exceeds ₹2,500 cr in preceding financial year, CCI pre-approval required.
If acquirer is non-resident, RBI approval for capital inflow and upstream remittance required.
